author: NDT Bureau
title: Trial of Michael Sang Correa for Torture Charges
text:
• Michael Sang Correa is accused of torturing individuals suspected of involvement in a failed coup against Gambia's leader Yahya Jammeh.
• Correa was a low-ranking private in the Gambian military and is charged under a U.S. law that allows prosecution for torture committed abroad.
• He was indicted in 2020 and faces six charges related to the torture of five people during the 2006 coup attempt.
• Correa served in a military unit known as the 'Junglers,' which reported directly to Yahya Jammeh.
• His lawyer argues that Correa acted under duress and did not have a choice in his actions.
• Federal prosecutors contend that Correa made choices to participate in the torture.
• One alleged victim was subjected to extreme torture, including being stuffed into a bag and dropped from a height.
• The prosecution's witness, Maggie Dwyer, provided context on Gambia's history and Jammeh's regime.
• Yahya Jammeh ruled Gambia for 22 years and was accused of human rights abuses, including torture and killings.
• Correa came to the U.S. as a bodyguard for Jammeh in December 2016 and overstayed his visa after Jammeh was ousted.
• Correa is the third person to be tried under the U.S. law for torture, following Charles Taylor, Jr. and Ross Roggio.
• Other countries have prosecuted individuals associated with Jammeh's regime for crimes against humanity.
